Strait of Hormuz Status: October 16, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
16 October 2026 .
Brent $ 109.69 + 3.56 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain reports UKMTO says most ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz go unreported, deepening the fog of war.

02 Brent settled at $109.69, up 3.56% in the last session before the close; WTI stood at $101.84.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The operational picture at the Strait of Hormuz is darker than the incident log suggests: gCaptain reports UKMTO has warned that most ship attacks are going unreported, and FreightWaves reports container ship attacks are escalating, meaning the documented toll understates the actual threat environment. CNBC reports Singapore-flagged ships have been attacked in the strait, and WWD and Yahoo report two ships have sunk near it as container vessel strikes intensify. A Newsquawk report, flagged as unverified and single-source, says an Indian shipping official described a crude oil tanker struck by a missile in the strait and referenced an October 14 Romania incident. Separately, Tehran Times, in an unverified single-source report, says Iran has reaffirmed the closure and says passage must be coordinated; the UAE-based Sawt al-Imarat, also unverified and single-source, reports the International Maritime Organization is seeking to resume navigation talks, without naming the parties. Brent settled at $109.69, up 3.56% in the last session before the close. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; the feed has carried 54 headlines in the last 24 hours. As of 21:22 UTC, 218 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
